schema: stops: lens (history|religion), year, lat, lon, caption, optional event (event slug), optional title

stops.caption: Han envoys open the western corridor from Chang’an.
stops.title: Han envoys

stops.caption: Rome, Parthia, Kushan and Han trade silk, glass and horses across Central Asia.
stops.title: Rome meets Han

stops.caption: Tang Chang’an is the eastern terminus of the busiest land route on earth.
stops.title: Tang Chang’an

stops.caption: The Mongol peace makes the whole road one jurisdiction.
stops.title: The Mongol peace

stops.caption: Constantinople falls; Europe turns to the sea routes.
stops.title: Constantinople falls

stops.caption: A small republic on the Tiber.
stops.title: A republic on the Tiber

stops.caption: The Ides of March: the republic ends in a dictator’s murder.
stops.title: The Ides of March

stops.caption: Trajan: the empire at its greatest extent.
stops.title: Trajan’s empire

stops.caption: The last western emperor is deposed at Ravenna.
stops.title: The fall of the West

stops.caption: The eastern empire falls with Constantinople.
stops.title: The fall of Constantinople

stops.caption: Berlin divided; two blocs face each other across Europe.
stops.title: Berlin divided

stops.caption: Cuba: the closest the world comes to nuclear war.
stops.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis

stops.caption: Vietnam and Prague: the blocs strain at both ends.
stops.title: Vietnam and Prague

stops.caption: The Wall comes down.
stops.title: The Wall comes down

stops.caption: The Soviet Union dissolves.
stops.title: The Soviet Union dissolves

tours.title: How a Jewish sect became Rome's religion
tours.thesis: How did a movement whose founder Rome executed become the only faith Roman law allowed?

stops.title: Crucifixion of Jesus
stops.caption: Pontius Pilate has Jesus of Nazareth scourged and crucified; his followers proclaim him risen and keep meeting in Jerusalem under James.

stops.title: Council of Jerusalem
stops.caption: A council in Jerusalem rules that Gentile converts need not be circumcised or keep the law of Moses.

stops.title: Great Fire of Rome
stops.caption: After fire burns much of Rome, Nero, says Tacitus, blames the Christians and begins the first persecution.

stops.title: Siege of Jerusalem (70 CE)
stops.caption: Titus's army of at least 48,200 destroys the Second Temple and razes Jerusalem.

stops.title: Decian persecution
stops.caption: Decius orders everyone to sacrifice before a magistrate and get a certificate; Pope Fabian dies refusing.

stops.title: Diocletianic Persecution
stops.caption: On 23 February 303, urged by Galerius, Diocletian begins the Great Persecution from Nicomedia, where the church overlooks his palace.

stops.title: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
stops.caption: Constantine defeats Maxentius, who drowns in the Tiber; Christian writers say a vision told him to fight under the Chi-Rho.
stops.source: "Battle of the Milvian Bridge," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Milvian_Bridge.

stops.title: Edict of Milan
stops.caption: Constantine and Licinius agree at Milan to treat Christians benevolently and allow religious freedom.

stops.title: First Council of Nicaea
stops.caption: Constantine calls the bishops to Nicaea over the Arian dispute; they write the first Nicene Creed.

stops.title: Edict of Thessalonica
stops.caption: Theodosius I makes Nicene Christianity the state church and brands other creeds heresy.

tours.title: From Miletus to Alexandria: Greek philosophy
tours.thesis: How did Greek philosophy, born in free trading cities, come to depend on the protection of kings?

stops.title: Eclipse of Thales
stops.caption: Thales, per Herodotus, predicts a solar eclipse; he seeks natural causes for things.

stops.title: Pythagoreanism
stops.caption: Pythagoras founds a brotherhood at Croton joining mathematics to a rule of life.

stops.title: Parmenides
stops.caption: Parmenides argues that change is illusion and only reason grasps what truly is.

stops.title: Trial of Socrates
stops.caption: Athens, recovering from defeat and oligarchic terror, condemns Socrates to death.

stops.title: Platonic Academy
stops.caption: Plato founds the Academy outside Athens.

stops.title: Aristotle
stops.caption: Philip II hires Aristotle to tutor his son Alexander.

stops.title: Lyceum (classical)
stops.caption: Aristotle opens the Lyceum and organizes research by subject.

stops.title: Stoicism
stops.caption: Zeno of Citium teaches in the Painted Stoa, founding Stoicism.

stops.title: Library of Alexandria
stops.caption: The Ptolemies fund the Museum and Library, a state research institute.

tours.title: Rise of Islam, 610-750
tours.thesis: How did a prophet's community in Arabia become an empire, and why did it fight itself over who should rule?

stops.title: Muhammad's first revelation
stops.caption: Muhammad reports his first revelation near Mecca.

stops.title: Hijrah
stops.caption: Facing persecution, Muhammad and followers move to Yathrib (Medina).

stops.title: Battle of Badr
stops.caption: A small Medinan force defeats a larger Meccan army.

stops.title: Conquest of Mecca
stops.caption: Mecca surrenders; the Kaaba's idols are destroyed.

stops.title: Saqifa
stops.caption: After Muhammad dies, Medinan and Meccan leaders choose Abu Bakr as caliph.

stops.title: Battle of the Yarmuk
stops.caption: Arab armies crush the Byzantines in Syria.

stops.title: Muslim conquest of Persia
stops.caption: The last Sasanian shah, Yazdegerd III, dies near Merv.

stops.title: First Fitna
stops.caption: Rebels kill Caliph Uthman, starting civil war between Ali and Muawiya.

stops.title: Umayyad Caliphate
stops.caption: Muawiya founds the Umayyad dynasty at Damascus.

stops.title: Battle of Karbala
stops.caption: Umayyad troops kill Husayn ibn Ali and his followers.

stops.title: Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula
stops.caption: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses into Iberia and destroys the Visigothic kingdom.
stops.source: "Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_conquest_of_the_Iberian_Peninsula.

stops.title: Battle of the Zab
stops.caption: Abbasid armies from Khurasan defeat the last Umayyad caliph.

tours.title: The Mongol Empire
tours.thesis: How did a steppe confederation build the largest land empire yet seen, and why did its own succession rule break it apart?

stops.title: Mongol Empire
stops.caption: A kurultai proclaims Temüjin as Genghis Khan of the united Mongols.

stops.title: Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty
stops.caption: Mongols take the Jin capital Zhongdu.
stops.source: "Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_conquest_of_the_Jin_dynasty.

stops.title: Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire
stops.caption: After Otrar's governor kills a Mongol caravan, Genghis invades Khwarazm.
stops.source: "Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_invasion_of_the_Khwarazmian_Empire.

stops.title: Genghis Khan
stops.caption: Genghis dies campaigning against Western Xia.

stops.title: Karakorum
stops.caption: Ögedei walls Karakorum as imperial capital.

stops.title: Battle of Mohi
stops.caption: Mongols rout the Hungarians; Ögedei then dies and the armies withdraw.

stops.title: Siege of Baghdad
stops.caption: Hülegü sacks Baghdad and kills the last Abbasid caliph.

stops.title: Battle of Ain Jalut
stops.caption: The Mamluks defeat a Mongol army in Galilee.

stops.title: Yuan dynasty
stops.caption: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty in China.

stops.title: Siege of Caffa
stops.caption: A Golden Horde army besieges Genoese Caffa as plague breaks out.

tours.title: The long fall of Constantinople
tours.thesis: Why did a city whose walls held for a thousand years fall in 1453?

stops.title: Battle of Manzikert
stops.caption: On 26 August the Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan destroys a Byzantine army and captures Emperor Romanos IV.

stops.title: Alexios I Komnenos
stops.caption: Alexios I's envoys ask Pope Urban II for help against the Seljuks; Urban calls the First Crusade.

stops.title: Sack of Constantinople
stops.caption: Unable to pay Venice for its fleet, the Fourth Crusade sacks Zara and then Constantinople, founding a Latin Empire.

stops.title: Reconquest of Constantinople
stops.caption: Alexios Strategopoulos and 800 men recover the city for Michael VIII, newly allied with Genoa.

stops.title: Gallipoli
stops.caption: An earthquake breaks Gallipoli's walls on 1-2 March; within a month the Ottomans hold their first base in Europe.

stops.title: Battle of Kosovo
stops.caption: On 15 June Murad I and Prince Lazar meet at Kosovo; both die.

stops.title: Battle of Ankara
stops.caption: Bayezid I breaks off his blockade of Constantinople to fight Timur, loses on 28 July and dies a captive.

stops.title: Battle of Varna
stops.caption: On 10 November Murad II destroys the crusade of Władysław III and John Hunyadi.

stops.title: Rumelihisarı
stops.caption: The young Mehmed II builds the 'strait-cutter' fortress on the Bosphorus.

stops.title: Fall of Constantinople
stops.caption: After a 53-day siege the city falls on 29 May; Constantine XI dies fighting.

tours.title: The Reformation and its wars
tours.thesis: When Western Christianity split, who decided what ordinary people would believe?

stops.title: Printing press
stops.caption: Gutenberg builds a movable-type press at Mainz.

stops.title: Ninety-five Theses
stops.caption: Angered by indulgences sold to rebuild St Peter's, Luther sends his theses to Archbishop Albert; printers make him Europe's most published author.

stops.title: Diet of Worms
stops.caption: Luther refuses to recant before Charles V; Elector Frederick has him 'kidnapped' to Wartburg Castle.

stops.title: German Peasants' War
stops.caption: Luther sides with the lords, who crush the peasants and kill up to 100,000.

stops.title: Augsburg Confession
stops.caption: On 25 June German rulers and cities present Melanchthon's confession to Charles V.

stops.title: Acts of Supremacy
stops.caption: Parliament makes Henry VIII 'the only supreme head on Earth' of the English church.

stops.title: Ecclesiastical Ordinances
stops.caption: Geneva adopts Calvin's Ordinances, with a Consistory to police doctrine and morals.

stops.title: Council of Trent
stops.caption: Paul III's council meets in 25 sessions from 1545 to 1563 to fix Catholic doctrine.

stops.title: Peace of Augsburg
stops.caption: After the Schmalkaldic War, each prince may make his land Lutheran or Catholic: cuius regio, eius religio.

stops.title: Defenestrations of Prague
stops.caption: On 23 May Bohemian Protestants throw two governors and a secretary from a castle window; all survive.

stops.title: Peace of Westphalia
stops.caption: Treaties at Münster and Osnabrück end the war and legally recognize Calvinism.

tours.title: The Age of Revolutions
tours.thesis: How did the cost of winning wars break three empires and carry revolution from Boston to Paris, Saint-Domingue and Caracas?

stops.title: Treaty of Paris (1763)
stops.caption: Britain wins the Seven Years' War, taking Canada and India footholds.

stops.title: Stamp Act 1765
stops.caption: Parliament taxes colonial paper documents.

stops.title: United States Declaration of Independence
stops.caption: Congress declares independence.
stops.source: "United States Declaration of Independence," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence.

stops.title: Treaty of Paris (1783)
stops.caption: Britain recognizes US independence.

stops.title: Storming of the Bastille
stops.caption: Crisis over royal debt ends with crowds storming the Bastille.

stops.title: Haitian Revolution
stops.caption: Enslaved people rise in northern Saint-Domingue.

stops.title: Haitian Declaration of Independence
stops.caption: Dessalines declares Haiti independent.

stops.title: Abdications of Bayonne
stops.caption: Napoleon forces the Spanish Bourbons to abdicate.

stops.title: Spanish American wars of independence
stops.caption: Juntas at Caracas, Buenos Aires and Bogotá take power.
stops.source: "Spanish American wars of independence," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_American_wars_of_independence.

stops.title: Battle of Ayacucho
stops.caption: Sucre defeats the last major Spanish army in Peru.

tours.title: Opium, trade and the Qing
tours.thesis: How did Britain's thirst for tea become a drug trade, two wars and a century of foreign power in China?

stops.title: Canton System
stops.caption: The Qing limit Western trade to Canton.

stops.title: Macartney Embassy
stops.caption: Qianlong rejects Britain's trade requests.

stops.title: First Opium War
stops.caption: The Qing court bans opium outright; in 1799 Canton's governor orders the trade halted, but smuggling goes on.

stops.title: Destruction of opium at Humen
stops.caption: Lin Zexu destroys 1,000 tonnes of seized opium.
stops.source: "Destruction of opium at Humen," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destruction_of_opium_at_Humen.

stops.title: Treaty of Nanking
stops.caption: The Qing cede Hong Kong and open five ports.

stops.title: Taiping Rebellion
stops.caption: Hong Xiuquan launches the Taiping Rebellion.

stops.title: Second Opium War
stops.caption: The Arrow incident starts a second war.

stops.title: Old Summer Palace
stops.caption: Troops loot and burn the Old Summer Palace.

stops.title: Self-Strengthening Movement
stops.caption: The Qing set up the Zongli Yamen and Self-Strengthening reforms.

stops.title: Boxer Rebellion
stops.caption: Boxers besiege the legations; foreign armies take Beijing.

tours.title: Decolonization
tours.thesis: How did Europe's empires lose within two generations the lands they had divided among themselves?

stops.title: Berlin Conference
stops.caption: Fourteen powers meeting in Berlin agree rules for claiming African territory by 'effective occupation'.

stops.title: Paris Peace Conference (1919–1920)
stops.caption: Wilson's talk of self-determination raises hopes, but the victors apply it only in Europe; petitions from colonial subjects, a young Ho Chi Minh among them, go unanswered.

stops.title: Atlantic Charter
stops.caption: Roosevelt and Churchill declare the right of all peoples to choose their form of government.

stops.title: Partition of India
stops.caption: A war-exhausted Britain hands power to India and Pakistan; partition kills hundreds of thousands and uproots millions.

stops.title: Indonesian National Revolution
stops.caption: After four years of war and US pressure, the Netherlands recognizes Indonesian sovereignty.

stops.title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
stops.caption: Viet Minh artillery forces the French garrison in northern Vietnam to surrender.
stops.source: "Battle of Dien Bien Phu," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Dien_Bien_Phu.

stops.title: Bandung Conference
stops.caption: Leaders of 29 Asian and African states, including Nehru, Sukarno and Nasser, meet at Bandung.

stops.title: Suez Crisis
stops.caption: Britain and France invade to retake the nationalized canal; US pressure on the pound forces them out.

stops.title: Gold Coast (British colony)
stops.caption: The Gold Coast becomes independent Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah, the first sub-Saharan colony to do so.

stops.title: Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples
stops.caption: In the 'Year of Africa' seventeen African states win independence, and the UN General Assembly declares colonial rule a denial of human rights.
stops.source: "Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_on_the_Granting_of_Independence_to_Colonial_Countries_and_Peoples.

stops.title: Évian Accords
stops.caption: France and the Algerian FLN sign the Évian Accords, ending the Algerian War.

tours.title: Money and central banking
tours.thesis: How did money pass from stamped metal to a government's promise, and who built the banks that keep it?

stops.title: Lydia
stops.caption: The kingdom of Lydia strikes the first known coins, lumps of electrum stamped with a royal guarantee.

stops.title: Liber Abaci
stops.caption: Leonardo of Pisa (Fibonacci) publishes the Liber Abaci, teaching Hindu-Arabic numerals and merchant arithmetic he learned in North Africa.

stops.title: Florin
stops.caption: Florence mints the gold florin, which holds its weight for centuries.

stops.title: Medici Bank
stops.caption: Giovanni di Bicci de' Medici founds the Medici Bank, which becomes the papacy's banker.

stops.title: Bank of Saint George
stops.caption: Genoa's state creditors form the Casa di San Giorgio, which collects taxes to service the city's debt.

stops.title: Bank of Amsterdam
stops.caption: The city of Amsterdam founds the Wisselbank to give merchants a stable bank money.

stops.title: Sveriges Riksbank
stops.caption: After the private Stockholms Banco fails, the Swedish parliament founds the Riksbank, the oldest surviving central bank.

stops.title: Bank of England
stops.caption: London investors lend £1.2 million to William III's war government and incorporate as the Bank of England.

stops.title: John Law's Company
stops.caption: John Law's Mississippi scheme collapses in Paris as the South Sea Bubble bursts in London.

stops.title: Federal Reserve Act
stops.caption: After the Panic of 1907, bankers and Congress create the Federal Reserve System.

stops.title: Bretton Woods Conference
stops.caption: Forty-four Allied nations peg their currencies to the dollar, and the dollar to gold at $35 an ounce.

stops.title: Nixon shock
stops.caption: Nixon suspends conversion of the dollar into gold.

tours.title: Papacy versus Empire
tours.thesis: Pope and emperor made each other; why did their fight over who stood higher end with kings on top?

stops.title: Donation of Pepin
stops.caption: Pepin the Short promises Pope Stephen II the lands taken from the Lombards, founding the Papal States.

stops.title: Charlemagne
stops.caption: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor in St Peter's on Christmas Day.

stops.title: Otto the Great
stops.caption: Pope John XII crowns Otto I emperor, reviving the western empire under German kings.

stops.title: Dictatus papae
stops.caption: Gregory VII asserts that the pope alone may depose emperors and appoint bishops.

stops.title: Road to Canossa
stops.caption: Henry IV waits in the snow at Canossa for Gregory's absolution.

stops.title: Concordat of Worms
stops.caption: Henry V and Calixtus II split investiture into spiritual and secular parts.

stops.title: Battle of Legnano
stops.caption: The Lombard League, allied with Pope Alexander III, defeats Frederick Barbarossa.

stops.title: Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor
stops.caption: Frederick II, excommunicated and declared deposed by the pope, dies at Castel Fiorentino in Apulia.
stops.source: "Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor," *Wikipedia*, accessed October 28, 2026, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_II,_Holy_Roman_Emperor.

stops.title: Unam sanctam
stops.caption: Boniface VIII declares that submission to the pope is necessary for salvation.

stops.title: Avignon Papacy
stops.caption: Clement V, a Gascon, settles the papal court at Avignon under French influence.

stops.title: Western Schism
stops.caption: Two, later three, rival popes divide Europe along political lines.

stops.title: Council of Constance
stops.caption: The council removes the rival popes and elects Martin V.

tours.title: Merchant republics to Amsterdam and London
tours.thesis: How did the center of European trade and credit move from Venice and Genoa to Amsterdam and London?

stops.title: Byzantine–Venetian treaty of 1082
stops.caption: Byzantium grants Venice tax-free trade across the empire in return for naval help against the Normans.

stops.title: Fourth Crusade
stops.caption: Doge Enrico Dandolo steers the Fourth Crusade into sacking Constantinople.

stops.title: Bardi family
stops.caption: The Bardi and Peruzzi banks collapse after heavy lending to Edward III and Florentine crises.

stops.title: Andrea Doria
stops.caption: Admiral Andrea Doria switches Genoa from France to Charles V.

stops.title: Philip II of Spain
stops.caption: Philip II suspends payments on his debts, the first of several Spanish defaults.

stops.title: Fall of Antwerp
stops.caption: Spanish forces take Antwerp; Protestant merchants must convert or leave, and many go to Amsterdam.

stops.title: Dutch East India Company
stops.caption: The States General charter the VOC, whose shares trade in Amsterdam.

stops.title: Rampjaar
stops.caption: France, England and two German bishoprics invade the Dutch Republic; William III takes power.

stops.title: Glorious Revolution
stops.caption: William III invades England with a Dutch fleet and takes the throne with Mary.

tours.title: How Buddhism spread
tours.thesis: How did a beggars' order cross Asia on the patronage of kings, and why did its wealth make it a target?

stops.title: The Buddha
stops.caption: Siddhartha Gautama is said to attain awakening under the Bodhi tree.

stops.title: The Buddha
stops.caption: The Buddha dies at Kushinagar.

stops.title: Kalinga War
stops.caption: The Mauryan emperor Ashoka conquers Kalinga at great cost in lives.

stops.title: Buddhist councils
stops.caption: Tradition places a Third Council under Ashoka at Pataliputra, which sends missions abroad.

stops.title: Kanishka
stops.caption: The Kushan emperor Kanishka patronises Buddhism and builds a great stupa at Peshawar.

stops.title: Lokaksema (Buddhist monk)
stops.caption: Lokaksema, a monk traditionally called Kushan, reaches Luoyang before Emperor Huan dies in January 168 and from 178 to 189 translates Mahayana sutras into Chinese.

stops.title: Goguryeo
stops.caption: The Former Qin court sends the monk Sundo with texts and images to Goguryeo.

stops.title: Buddhism in Japan
stops.caption: Baekje's king sends a Buddha image and sutras to the Yamato court.

stops.title: Huichang persecution of Buddhism
stops.caption: Tang emperor Wuzong closes thousands of monasteries and seizes their wealth.
